questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Understanding and speaking the language of my destination. Clinical rotation is not lectures with professors who speak English, it's talking to doctors and patients, and both are more comfortable explaining in their native language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything but the academic aspect was a 10!

questions.answer: Very easy, the university coordinator at UiB was very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived 3 days before the first day of the clinic. I only received help when I started my clinical rotation.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I looked through old reviews and saw that medical students before me had stayed in Haukelandsbakken Studentheim right next to the hospital. It was really easy, I wrote them an email in june and was assured there would be available housing. It's very dorm-like, with shared toilets, showers and a kitchen. However, the people there are nice, it's quiet, no partying until 5 in the morning, and it took me 8 minutes to walk to the hospital. I paid 3200 NOK for housing/month. The university offers accomodations most commonly at "Fantoft student housing", but they are more expensive and are approximately 30 minutes away from the hospital by light rail as well as 45-50 minutes away from the city centre.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you do a clinical rotation it choose a place where you live with other people. You won't have lectures where you meet other students, so it can become very lonely. I chose a dorm, and it was perfect.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Marte (the university coordinator) sent clear instructions per mail and answered any questions I had very quickly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received a log-in to their student website and had to register. Because I had clinical rotation and no courses I did not have to sign up for courses. I think the deadline was september 1st.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Marte the university coordinator was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just write them an email if you're unsure of what to do.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
When I had to register the university coordinator asked where I wanted to spend the clinical rotation, and I sent a list of 5 departments. I thought I was going to be at several departments during my 12 week stay, but I was only placed in one. This was the department of plastic surgery and burn victims. It was very interesting to be there, but unfortunately I did not receive any kind of tutoring plan, plan for the weeks or even a tutor doctor which I was supposed to have. Despite having requested this to the chief doctor (?) Hans Christian Sylvester-Jensen, several times, as well as sending 4 (!) emails to the department, these conditions were never met. The chief doctor even said to me in my third week "Well, we can't really make a plan for you, we can't spend time on that." which I find to be not only unprofessional but lazy as fuck.
If you are going to Haukeland Sjukehus DO NOT choose plastic surgery. 
I love surgery and I got to do a lot of stuff and be part of some really cool operations but I had to ask and doing that 50 times a day for 12 weeks is really exhausting. In comparison my Swedish friend was at three different departments and had plans made for her in two of those.
Overall I wasn't impressed with the academic aspect of the stay.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Had to buy duvet and pillow for my room when I arrived, so had an unexpectedly long trip to IKEA by bus and paid for stuff I wasn't sure I could bring home to DK again.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive, but the NOK is very low right now, so that did help. I spent a lot of time on cafés and therefore a lot of money on coffee :) A good cappucino is only 30-35 DKK!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any, I don't know if there were any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Well, as mentioned I spent a lot of time at cafés and not really in any student communities. If the weather is nice go hiking! Ulriken is very pretty, Fløyen as well. Walk around the city. 
I went to Hardness skogen to pick mushrooms but found out later that the forest beneath Ulriken was overflowing with funnel chantarelles.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Went on a boat trip to Flåm, 5,5 hours, can recommend as well. Then took the train from Flåm-Myrdal, Myrdal-Voss, Voss-Bergen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Norway is very much like Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't, so no, sorry.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really, we are very alike.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of help from one nurse and a doctor at the hospital with planning my trip home from Norway. I drove with my friend in a car all the way home through Sweden. They helped me plan the trip and one of them even had a discount for a hotel that she shared with me.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring an umbrella. Do it. It rains all the time. And waterproof everything. You can buy it there, but if you have it, bring it.
Be open, enjoy your free time, don't spend it at the hospital, go see the city you live in. Don't be afraid to experience things alone if you don't have anyone to go with.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you like collecting mushrooms they have an app as well as physical "mushroom control groups" called "Soppkontroll". Mushrooms experts go through your basket and make sure you don't have any toxic ones.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing another climate, another city and another healthcare system.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling like I wasn't welcome or wanted at the hospital, and like I was really just a burden...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go go go. As I wrote, everything about my stay except the hospital department was 10/10!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
